decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach with open grippers, rotating toward top-down grasps; estimate object positions from calibrated head view.
Reduce initial increments to preserve IK joint continuity after zero-step rejection.
Move above inner chocolate and black watch while completing downward wrist orientation; keep elevation for visual alignment.
Refine alignment from wrist views: table appears higher than first estimate; shift inward over chocolate and black watch, with small orientation corrections.
Fine-center both visible objects between open jaws and lower gradually to grasp height.
Chocolate shifted on contact: lift and realign for its new long axis. Close right gripper around watch and lift to test visible retention.
Follow displaced chocolate without contacting it; return jaw alignment across its width. Lift the closed right grasp and start toward the middle basket.
Lower left fingers around narrow dimension of chocolate; transport visibly retained black watch to the right half of the middle basket.
Use smaller inward steps for right-arm continuity while approaching middle basket. Continue controlled left descent.
Adjust right wrist tilt and slightly lower/retract to recover reach margin before lateral transfer. Close left jaws at chocolate height.
Lift left grasp to verify which object is retained; carry black watch laterally over blue basket using tilted wrist for reach and rim clearance.
Left grasp was empty; reopen and approach chocolate lower across its narrow dimension. Release visibly retained watch well inside the middle blue basket.
Watch is visible in blue basket. Shift left grasp away from adjacent pepper, close on chocolate, and route open right arm back toward the second watch.
Retry unexecuted retreat with smaller right-arm increments while isolating and closing left chocolate grasp.
Lift closed left grasp to inspect retention and possible pepper interference; bring right arm above remaining watch.
Switch left to isolated outer chocolate and rotate jaws across its short axis. Align and descend over remaining watch with right.
Use wrist alignment to center outer chocolate at lower height; center and close on brown watch.
Center and close across chocolate width at a slightly lower height, then test lift. Lift retained brown watch and tilt for transport.
Transport the visually retained chocolate toward white basket and brown watch toward blue, keeping grippers closed and tilting for reach.
Left chocolate was not retained; return open jaws with corrected along-bar alignment. Continue right watch to the middle basket.
Release second watch inside blue basket. Correct left lateral alignment and descend further before closing on the thin chocolate.
Close centered chocolate grasp at tabletop clearance and dwell before lifting. Move right above green pepper while restoring downward orientation.
Carry confirmed chocolate grasp above white basket with clearance; lower and close right gripper around green pepper.
Lift chocolate clear of front rim before advancing further. Lift green pepper in right grasp while retaining both objects.
Reconcile left orientation with preceding accepted target while lifting, after continuity rejection; keep both grasps closed.
First chocolate is visible in white basket. Approach remaining chocolate open-handed; carry retained green pepper above red basket with rim clearance.
Release green pepper inside red basket; descend left jaws on the near end of remaining chocolate, avoiding adjacent yellow pepper.
Close and dwell on remaining chocolate, then test retention by lifting. Reposition right arm on its side near the remaining yellow pepper.
Carry retained second chocolate over white basket. Approach yellow pepper from right with a modest inward wrist tilt, keeping arms on their own sides.
Release second chocolate into white basket and withdraw left. Fine-center tilted right grasp and descend around remaining yellow pepper.
Close and test-lift yellow pepper with right while beginning unobstructed left-arm reset.
Transport retained yellow pepper toward red basket. Retract left arm while checking basket contents; a wrapper may have shifted outside white basket.
Yellow pepper slipped and chocolate is visibly outside white basket. Reapproach both displaced objects with open jaws for recovery.
Back right gripper away from basket rim before descending. Approach escaped chocolate from left exterior, rotating jaw axis without changing forward tilt.
Lower tilted left grasp toward escaped bar outside basket. Center right gripper over yellow pepper away from rim and descend.
Close both recovery grasps, dwell, and lift vertically before any sideways transport to check retention.
Lift yellow pepper fully above basket rim before translating. Retry chocolate with more vertical jaw alignment while maintaining elbow configuration.
Carry yellow pepper over red basket at full rim clearance. Reorient left tilt along chocolate length so both jaws can reach its thin sides.
Recover left reach margin after interrupted approach by moving inward before reorientation. Place yellow pepper inside red basket, with open release after clearing rim.
Both peppers now visible in red basket. Withdraw right arm and reposition left outside white wall for a lower, partially closed chocolate recovery.
Use smaller right retreat increments after zero-step continuity rejection; move left clear of basket wall for chocolate recovery.
Narrow left opening before lowering through the tilted grasp to avoid one open finger blocking on tabletop. Continue right-arm reset clear of sorted objects.
Correct missed left pinch toward the bar using a narrower opening and lower approach; continue gradual right reset.
Shift left pinch onto visible bar rather than beside it, lifting slightly to free tabletop contact. Finish gentle right reset.
Close jaws on the now-centered chocolate, dwell, then make a small test lift; right arm remains at origin.
Tilted pinch is not retaining the thin bar. Gently draw it toward the reachable near side with closed fingertips, keeping away from basket contents.
Bar rotated into a more accessible direction; switch to a near-vertical grasp on its near end while avoiding basket wall and extension limit.
Use calibrated head and wrist alignment to center the near end of the displaced chocolate for a nearly vertical pinch.
Pinch the aligned near end of the chocolate and lift with simultaneous retraction to preserve reach margin; verify retention visually.
Chocolate now appears pinched at its near end. Lift clear of the basket wall while retracting to maintain elbow-up reach margin.
One chocolate is visible inside the white basket; the other slipped outside. Approach its center with level jaw heights and a forward tilt for reach.
Narrow jaws to clear the basket wall, move onto the middle of the bar, and close at a lower grasp height.
Lift the centered chocolate grasp above the basket rim with slight retraction, keeping closed throughout.
Confirmed chocolate retention: raise a little more for rim clearance, then translate over the center of the left basket without changing grasp orientation.
Release chocolate while stationary over white basket, allow it to settle, then begin a slow retreat without disturbing contents.
Both chocolates are now visible in white, both watches in blue, and both peppers in red. Return left arm gradually to origin with open jaws and refine right reset.
Continue smooth left-arm return to origin, preserving elbow-up configuration; right remains reset and baskets undisturbed.
Finish gradual left-arm reset to its starting pose with both grippers open; apply only tiny right-origin corrections.
